title: Williams v. City of Detroit (Face Recognition False Arrest) — case page
bias_or_interest: ACLU is Williams' counsel. Factual assertions about its own client are party statements; the arrest narrative and evidence chain are independently corroborated by NYT/NPR/MIT Tech Review (SRC-0004/0005/0006) and the Wayne County prosecutor's public dismissal/apology.
relevant_locations: Arrest circumstances (driveway, in front of wife and daughters, ~30 hours in custody); evidence chain (surveillance still -> DataWorks Plus -> state license photo -> photo lineup to a loss-prevention contractor who had seen only the video); lawsuit filing (April 2021, E.D. Mich.); 'first publicly reported' framing; June 28, 2024 settlement and required reforms.
quotation_note: ACLU frames Williams as 'the first publicly reported instance' of a wrongful arrest from a facial-recognition match — quotable as 'first publicly reported' / 'first known,' NOT 'first ever' (see SRC-0009 flag: Oliver and Parks were arrested chronologically earlier).
rights_note: Cite as official/party source; corroborate legal and numeric claims with primary court records and independent reporting.
notes: Anchor source for person/arrest facts (CLM-0001/0002), evidence chain (CLM-0004), lawsuit (CLM-0008), settlement reforms (CLM-0009), and the 'first publicly reported' framing (CLM-0011). fact_recheck: the exact $300,000 figure is NOT on this page (see SRC-0010); confirm verbatim policy language against the settlement PDF (SRC-0003).

title: Civil Rights Advocates Achieve the Nation's Strongest Police Department Policy on Facial Recognition Technology (press release)
bias_or_interest: ACLU press release announcing its own settlement. 'Nation's strongest' is the ACLU's characterization and must be attributed, not stated as neutral fact. The specific policy terms are drawn from the court-filed settlement (SRC-0003).
relevant_locations: Settlement date (June 28, 2024); policy restrictions (no arrest on a facial-recognition result alone; no lineup immediately after an FR search; FR result is an investigative lead only; disclosure to courts/defense; officer training including higher misidentification of people of color; audit of every case since 2017 where FR was used to seek a warrant; court retains enforcement jurisdiction for four years).
quotation_note: Attribute 'the nation's strongest' policy to the ACLU. The reform terms themselves are assertable as the settlement's content, corroborated by SRC-0001/SRC-0003.
rights_note: Cite as official/party source; corroborate with the settlement document (SRC-0003).
notes: Primary basis for the 2024 settlement reforms (CLM-0009). Does NOT state the dollar figure (CLM-0010 rests on SRC-0010).

title: Final Order of Dismissal and Settlement Agreement, Williams v. City of Detroit (E.D. Mich., filed June 2024) + ACLU one-page summary
author: United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan (settlement filed by the parties)
organization: U.S. District Court, E.D. Mich. / ACLU (summary)
bias_or_interest: Court-filed settlement agreement — authoritative primary document for the exact monetary figure and verbatim policy language. Filed by the parties (including plaintiff's counsel) but entered by the court.
relevant_locations: Verbatim settlement terms: monetary payment to Williams plus attorneys' fees; the facial-recognition policy restrictions; the 2017-onward case audit; four-year court enforcement window.
quotation_note: Authoritative source for the exact $300,000 figure and the exact policy wording. NOTE: the PDF body text was not machine-rendered during research; lock verbatim quotes and the dollar figure against this document before publish.
rights_note: Public court record; the ACLU-hosted PDF is a copy. Public domain as a judicial filing.
notes: Primary basis for CLM-0009/CLM-0010. fact_recheck [BLOCKING-BEFORE-PUBLISH]: render the PDF and confirm the $300,000 amount and verbatim policy terms; until confirmed, narration hedges the amount as 'reported' and quotes policy terms in paraphrase.

title: Wrongfully Accused by an Algorithm
author: Kashmir Hill
bias_or_interest: Contemporaneous investigative reporting of record; independent of the parties. First national account of the case.
relevant_locations: Williams' full name and residence (Farmington Hills, Mich.); the Shinola theft; DataWorks Plus software; the old driver's-license photo match; the loss-prevention contractor who identified him from a lineup having seen only the video; the ~30-hour detention; 'first known' framing; the Wayne County prosecutor's apology and dismissal.
quotation_note: Headline is directly quotable (grade-A): 'Wrongfully Accused by an Algorithm.' Use as the independent corroboration that makes the arrest/evidence facts more than a party claim.
rights_note: Quote the headline as reported fact; do not reproduce full article text.
notes: Anchor independent source for CLM-0001/0002/0004 and the 'first known' framing (CLM-0011). Direct fetch was rate-limited during research; facts corroborated via NPR (SRC-0005) and MIT Tech Review (SRC-0006).

title: 'The Computer Got It Wrong': How Facial Recognition Led To A False Arrest In Michigan
author: Bobby Allyn
bias_or_interest: Independent national broadcaster; contemporaneous corroboration of the NYT account.
relevant_locations: The arrest, the facial-recognition match, the evidence chain, and the eventual dismissal; independent corroboration of SRC-0004.
quotation_note: Title phrase 'The Computer Got It Wrong' is quotable/attributable. Use for corroboration, not as sole basis.

title: The new lawsuit that shows facial recognition is officially a civil rights issue
author: Tate Ryan-Mosley
bias_or_interest: Independent technology journalism; reports the April 2021 lawsuit and the underlying facts in detail.
relevant_locations: October 2018 Shinola theft (~$3,800, five watches); March 2019 facial-recognition search; DataWorks Plus; January 9, 2020 arrest; 'first documented example' framing; the April 2021 lawsuit.
quotation_note: Source for the precise theft figures and the March 2019 search / Jan 9 2020 arrest dates. These specific figures rest mainly here plus wire copy (grade-B) — attribute to reporting; keep narration hedged where a single-strong-secondary carries the number.
notes: Basis for CLM-0003 (theft figures, grade-B) and CLM-0008 (lawsuit); corroborates CLM-0004. fact_recheck: 'October 2018 / five watches / ~$3,800' and 'March 2019 search' before locking on-screen figures.

title: Face Recognition Vendor Test (FRVT) Part 3: Demographic Effects (NISTIR 8280) + NIST news summary
author: Patrick Grother, Mei Ngan, Kayee Hanaoka
organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (U.S. Department of Commerce)
bias_or_interest: U.S. government standards laboratory; independent, methodologically transparent. Study scale: 189 algorithms from 99 developers, 18.27M images from government databases.
relevant_locations: One-to-one matching: higher false-positive rates for Asian and African American faces relative to Caucasian, differentials 'a factor of 10 to 100'; one-to-many matching: higher false positives for African American females; counter-finding that algorithms developed in Asia did not show the Asian-vs-Caucasian gap (effect tied to training data).
quotation_note: Quote NIST's own neutral language: 'higher rates of false positives for Asian and African American faces relative to images of Caucasians,' differentials 'often ranged from a factor of 10 to 100 times.' Always pair with the Asia-developed counter-finding; present as measured false-positive differentials, never as 'the technology is racist.'
notes: Primary basis for the accuracy-gap claim (CLM-0006). One-to-many is the mode relevant to police database searches.

title: Gender Shades: Intersectional Accuracy Disparities in Commercial Gender Classification
author: Joy Buolamwini, Timnit Gebru
organization: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, Vol. 81 (1st Conf. on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency) / MIT Media Lab
bias_or_interest: Peer-reviewed academic study. Note: it measures GENDER CLASSIFICATION (labeling a face male/female) in three commercial systems, a related but DISTINCT task from the identity-matching used in the Williams arrest.
relevant_locations: Error rates: 'Darker-skinned females are the most misclassified group (with error rates of up to 34.7%). The maximum error rate for lighter-skinned males is 0.8%.'
quotation_note: Cite both endpoints (34.7% vs 0.8%) and state explicitly it is gender-classification error, corroborating demographic performance gaps — do NOT present it as the identity-matching error rate that produced Williams' arrest.
rights_note: Cite academic source; quote the two figures.
notes: Corroborating basis for CLM-0007 (demographic performance gap), framed as a distinct task from face matching.

title: More than a Dozen Wrongful Arrests Due to Police Reliance on Facial Recognition Technology
author: Lauren Yu, Nathan Freed Wessler
bias_or_interest: ACLU advocacy tally. The existence of individual later cases (Oliver, Parks, Woodruff) is corroborated by independent outlets; the aggregate 'more than a dozen' is a single advocacy count and must be attributed.
relevant_locations: Roster of later wrongful-arrest cases (Michael Oliver, Nijeer Parks, Porcha Woodruff — arrested while eight months pregnant, and others); the 'more than a dozen documented' aggregate; the note that Oliver and Parks were arrested chronologically before Williams' case surfaced.
quotation_note: Report the total as 'at least a dozen documented cases (by the ACLU's count).' Use to establish 'not the last' and to correctly qualify 'first PUBLICLY REPORTED' (Oliver/Parks were arrested earlier but surfaced later).
rights_note: Cite as advocacy/party tally; attribute the aggregate.
notes: Basis for the 'not the last' beat (CLM-0012) and the hedge on CLM-0011. Grade-A for existence of Oliver/Parks; grade-B for the aggregate count.

title: Faulty Facial Recognition Tech Got Him Arrested. Now He's Getting a $300,000 Payout (and corroborating wire coverage)
author: Joe Lancaster (Reason); Associated Press / TechTimes syndication
bias_or_interest: Independent secondary outlets and the AP wire, all reporting the $300,000 payment. The figure is NOT stated on the ACLU case page/press release, so it rests on multiply-independent secondary reporting pending confirmation against the settlement PDF (SRC-0003).
relevant_locations: The $300,000 monetary payment to Williams as part of the June 2024 settlement (plus attorneys' fees), reported uniformly across Reason, TechTimes, and AP-syndicated coverage.
quotation_note: Assertable as 'a settlement reported at three hundred thousand dollars.' Keep the 'reported' hedge until the settlement PDF (SRC-0003) is rendered and the figure confirmed.
rights_note: Cite as independent secondary reporting; corroborate with the primary settlement document before locking.
notes: Basis for CLM-0010 (grade-B, hedged). fact_recheck [BEFORE-PUBLISH]: confirm $300,000 against SRC-0003.
